title: Build your first MCP server
description: Expose one local, read-only tool with a clear schema and error behavior.
prerequisites: MCP introduction, Python, and tool calling.
objectives: Implement a small SDK-based stdio server
Verify tool discovery, valid inputs, and missing records
explanation: Start with one deterministic read-only capability over invented data. Give the tool a specific name, a short description, typed inputs, and documented output behavior. The SDK handles protocol framing; your handler remains responsible for validation and application permissions.

The supplied example follows the official Python MCPServer API documented for the 2026-07-28 protocol generation. Create an isolated environment, install a compatible mcp release, and save its exact installed version with the exercise. Launch the file through an MCP client using the environment Python executable and the absolute script path.

Use stdio for this local exercise. Standard output carries protocol messages, so send diagnostic logs to standard error. In a compatible inspector or host, list tools, invoke lookup_stock with SKU-1, then test an unknown SKU and invalid input. Record expected and observed outcomes before adding a second capability.

terms.definition: Reading the operations and schemas a server exposes.
Protocol communication through a launched process standard streams.
A library that implements protocol machinery for an application.

example: mcp_inventory.py exposes stock counts for two invented SKUs. SKU-1 returns five units; an unknown SKU produces a clear tool error. The server has no filesystem search, network access, or inventory-write operation in its handler.
mistakes: Printing debugging messages to protocol stdout.
Assuming a server command uses the same Python environment as a terminal.
Copying an SDK import from a different major version.
exercise: Create a separate virtual environment, install the compatible MCP SDK, and connect the sample through an MCP inspector. Verify discovery, SKU-1, an unknown SKU, and a non-string argument. Capture results without logging credentials.

code.title: A small read-only inventory server
code.note: Optional integration example using the documented MCPServer API. Requires a compatible mcp SDK and MCP client. The network-free output checks do not verify a live protocol session.

questions.question: Why start an MCP server with one read-only tool?
questions.answer: A narrow deterministic capability is easier to validate before expanding scope.
questions.distractor: Read-only tools do not need input validation.

questions.question: Where should a stdio server write diagnostic logs?
questions.answer: To standard error so protocol messages on standard output remain intact.
questions.distractor: Into arbitrary lines on standard output.

questions.question: The host reports an import error but the script works in a terminal. What should you compare?
questions.answer: The exact Python executable, installed SDK version, and absolute script path.

questions.question: What should be tested besides a successful tool call?
questions.answer: Discovery, schema validation, missing records, and defined error behavior.
questions.distractor: Nothing; one successful call proves all behavior.

questions.question: Does the SDK decide which user may access a real inventory record?
questions.answer: No. Application identity and resource authorization remain your responsibility.
questions.distractor: Yes, a tool decorator grants correct access automatically.
